title: Mechanical conditioning of human mesenchymal stem cells for enhancing vascular regeneration
protocol: Thaw hMSCs at 37°C.
Add 10 mL of warm hMSC media.
Centrifuge hMSC at 300G for 3 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Aspirate culture media.
Add 10 mL of warm hMSC media.
Resuspend cells thoroughly.
Seed hMSC in T75 flask.
Passage hMSC at 70%–80% confluence.
Check cell confluency under a microscope.
Warm cell culture media, PBS, and 0.05% Trypsin-EDTA at 37°C.
Aspirate culture media.
Wash cells with 5 mL sterile PBS with 30 μM of HEPES.
Add 5 mL of warm 0.05% Trypsin-EDTA and incubate for 3 min at 37°C.
Add 5 mL of warm cell culture media to deactivate trypsin-EDTA.
Centrifuge at 300 G for 3 minutes at room temperature.
Aspirate the culture media.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL of warm hMSC media.
Count cells using a hemacytometer.
Prepare cell density to be 40,000 cells/mL.
Seed cells into a T75 flask.
Monitor cells daily for growth.
Change media completely every other day.
Apply mechanical stretching to the cells using a custom-built or commercial device for biomechanical conditioning over 9 days.
Deliver an EGFR/ERBB-2/4 inhibitor (CAS#:881001-19-0) to the cells during the weeklong biomechanical conditioning.
UV sterilize completed stretch plates overnight (∼12 h).
Coat plates with 50 μg/mL fibronectin overnight (∼12 h) at 37°C.
Remove fibronectin solution gently.
Wash plates once with 1 mL sterile PBS.
Aspirate culture media and wash cells once with 4 mL of sterile PBS.
Add 3 mL of warm 0.05% Trypsin-EDTA and incubate for 3 min at 37°C.
Add 10 mL of warm MSC media to deactivate trypsin-EDTA.
Resuspend cells thoroughly and collect cell suspension in a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300G for 3 min.
Aspirate media from the 15 mL tube.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL MSC media.
Count cells using a hemacytometer.
Adjust the concentration of the cell suspension to generate required seeding density for a 6 well plate: Add media to achieve a density of 95,000 cells/mL.
Seed 2 mL/well in a 6 well plate at a density of 95,000 cells/mL.
Adjust the concentration of the cell suspension to generate required seeding density for a 96 well plate: Add media to achieve a density of 43,000 cells/mL.
Seed 150 μL/well in a 96 well plate at a density of 43,000 cells/mL.
Let cells attach and grow overnight (∼12 h) in a 37°C 5% CO2 cell culture incubator.
Aspirate media and replace with fresh MSC media + 1 μM EGFR/ERBB-2/4 inhibitor.
Attach stretch plate to machine.
Tighten outer screws.
Tighten inner screws.
Start water coolant system.
Run at 15°C during stretching of cells.
Stretch cells.
Apply brachial waveform mechanical loading at 7.5% maximal strain, 0.1 Hz for 4 hours per day for 7 days.
Replace culture media with fresh MSC media and E/E inhibitor every other day.
Collect hMSCs from stretch plates.
Thaw accutase at 4°C overnight (∼12 h).
Rinse cells with PBS.
Aspirate PBS.
Add accutase to cells.
Incubate cells with accutase at RT for 5–10 min.
Use cell scraper to detach cells.
Collect cells into a FACS tube.
Use cell strainer on a tube.
Keep tubes on ice.
Centrifuge cells at 4°C for 4 min at 400 G.
Aspirate supernatant.
Count cells using hemacytometer.
Add 150,000 cells to each flow cytometry tube.
Add surface staining antibodies in BD stain buffer.
Include 1 tube of unstained cells as a negative control.
Incubate cells at 4°C for 30 min.
Add 1 mL of stain buffer to the tube.
Centrifuge cells at 4°C for 4 min at 400 G.
Aspirate supernatant.
Prepare fix/perm solution according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Add 1 mL of fix/perm solution.
Pipette up and down to break up pellet.
Incubate the solution at 4°C for 50 min.
Prepare perm/wash buffer according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Wash cells with 1 mL of perm/wash buffer.
Centrifuge cells at 4°C for 4 min at 400 G.
Aspirate supernatant.
Add 5 μL of nestin antibody in BD stain buffer.
Add BD stain buffer with the antibody to cells.
Pipette up and down to break pellet.
Incubate cells at 4°C for 50 min.
Wash cells again with 1 mL of perm/wash buffer.
Centrifuge cells at 4°C for 4 min at 400 G.
Aspirate supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 500 μL of stain buffer.
Cover samples with aluminum foil to prevent exposure to light.
Analyze MSC phenotype by flow cytometry.
Prepare compensation controls.
Mix one droplet of positive mouse IG beads and one droplet of negative mouse IG beads in each flow tube.
Add 80 μL of stain buffer to each tube.
Add 20 μL of each mouse IG fluorescence to each tube.
Pipette up and down to mix thoroughly.
Incubate beads at 4°C for 30 min.
Add 1 mL of stain buffer to each tube.
Centrifuge beads at 4°C for 4 min at 400 G.
Aspirate supernatant.
Add 1 mL of fix/perm solution to each tube.
Pipette up and down to break pellet.
Incubate beads at 4°C for 50 min.
Add 1 mL of stain buffer to wash beads.
Centrifuge beads at 4°C for 4 min at 400 G.
Aspirate supernatant.
Repeat washing process three more times.
Resuspend beads in 500 μL of stain buffer.
Set fluorescence in compensation window.
Adjust the filter configuration of flow cytometry system to match fluorescent spectra and minimize spectral overlap.
Adjust voltages for FSC and SSC channels using an unstained MSC control sample to set the position of the cell population.
Adjust voltages for fluorescence channels using an unstained MSC control sample so that the intensity of the unstained group is lower than 103.
Adjust voltages for each fluorescence channel using each IG control beads so that the peak of each channel is around 104.
Set gate around the peak.
Mix in unstained beads to assure that the background peak is well spaced from the positive peak.
Measure samples to analyze phenotype and count at least 10,000 events per tube.
Make scatterplot and set FSC-A on X-axis and SSC-A on Y-axis with endothelial cell data.
Gate for the population of cells to exclude debris and large particles.
Select gated population, then plot SSC-A on X-axis versus SSC-H on Y-axis.
Gate for the population of single cells to exclude doublets and large particles.
Select gated population, then plot FSC-A on X-axis versus FSC-H on Y-axis.
Gate for the population of single cells to exclude doublets.
Select gated population, then plot PDGFRβ on X-axis versus PECAM-1 on Y-axis.
Gate for the population of cells to separate endothelial phenotype from vSMCs, pericyte, undifferentiated MSCs, and the hybrid phenotype.
Repeat steps A-G with vSMC data to confirm vSMC phenotype.
Repeat steps A-G with pericyte data to separate pericyte phenotype from the other phenotypes.
Gate for the population of cells that only express PDGFRβ.
Plot NG2 on X-axis versus CD146 on Y-axis.
Gate for the population of cells that express both markers.
Plot FSC-A on X-axis versus Nestin on Y-axis.
Gate for the population of cells to confirm pericyte phenotype.
Perform gating analysis in Flowjo software for mechanically conditioned cells.
Make scatterplot and set FSC-A on X-axis and SSC-A on Y-axis.
Gate for the population of cells to exclude debris and large particles.
Select gated population, then plot SSC-A on X-axis versus SSC-H on Y-axis.
Gate for the population of single cells to exclude doublets and large particles.
Select gated population, then plot FSC-A on X-axis versus FSC-H on Y-axis.
Gate for the population of single cells to exclude doublets.
Select gated population, then plot PDGFRβ on X-axis versus PECAM-1 on Y-axis.
Gate for the population of cells that express both markers to separate the hybrid phenotype from endothelial cells, vSMCs, pericyte, and undifferentiated MSCs.
Select gated population.
Plot CD105 on X-axis versus CD144 on Y-axis.
Gate for the population of cells that express both CD105 and CD144 markers.
Plot Nestin on X-axis versus CD146 on Y-axis.
Gate for the population of cells that express both Nestin and CD146 markers.
Plot FSC-A on X-axis versus NG2 on Y-axis.
Gate for the population of cells that express the pericyte marker NG2.
Export the frequency of the population and statistics in the table editor to draw graphs.
Prepare alginate solution 1 day in advance: mix 2% alginate solution (2g alginate per 100 mL sterile saline) with 2% alginate:RGD in a 1:5 ratio.
Supplement alginate solution with 0.045% type 1 collagen.
Mix extremely well and keep on ice or at 4°C.
Prepare calcium chloride solution: mix 1.1% CaCl2 in ultrapure water.
Autoclave sterile water and sterile surgical saline solutions.
Rinse and autoclave feeder tubes for gel extruder parts.
Soak extruder parts in 70% ethanol and leave overnight at ∼12 h.
Assemble gel extruder pieces in the sterile cell culture hood.
Load device with 70% ethanol.
Let air dry for 30 min.
Cover syringe feeder tube with ice and place syringes in 4°C refrigerator before beginning.
Pump air through entire system to ensure it is unclogged.
Remove culture media from 6 well stretch plates.
Wash cells once with PBS.
Treat cells with warmed 0.05% Trypsin-EDTA for less than 5 min to detach cells.
Centrifuge cells 300G for 5 min.
Resuspend cells in 1 ml room temperature (20°C–25°C) PBS and count them with a hemacytometer.
Centrifuge cells 300G for 5 min.
Resuspend 1 × 10^6 cells in 200 μL (5 × 10^6 cells/mL) of alginate solution.
Prepare slightly more than 200 μL in syringe, at least 250 μL or more per mouse.
Prime encapsulator tube with alginate and cell solution, keep tube on ice.
Prime until alginate solution drips into waste dish.
Fill syringe with air to push alginate solution through tube.
Load syringe onto syringe pump and lock in place.
Replace waste dish with clean dish containing calcium chloride solution.
Adjust the secondary valve slowly until flow reaches 3 L/min.
Begin flowing syringe pump at 0.1 mL/min, ensuring that the syringe is locked in place.
Collect alginate beads in calcium chloride solution; beads should have a diameter of 1,200 μm.
Pause syringe pump once 200 μL of solution is extruded.
Remove CaCl2 and wash beads with sterile saline 2–3 times.
Collect beads using 50 mL serological pipette and transport to animal.
Tip: Prepare separate saline syringe to flush extruder if it becomes clogged.
Anesthetize mice with 2%–5% isoflurane for 1–2 min.
Mask and maintain mouse on 2%–5% isoflurane for duration of procedure.
Shave surgical site: left hindlimb.
Scrub surgical site with three cycles of betadine scrub followed by alcohol rinse.
Lay down fresh autoclaved absorbent surgical pads for sterile field use.
Anesthetize mice with 2%–5% isoflurane for 1–2 min.
Mask and maintain mouse on 2%–5% isoflurane throughout the procedure.
Test adequate anesthesia with withdrawal to simulation in toe pinch test.
Inject 10 mg/kg carprofen subcutaneously at least 30 min before the end of the procedure.
Check adequate anesthesia every 15 min during procedure.
Make a skin incision on the medial side of the thigh of the left hindlimb.
Dissect femoral artery free without damaging vein and nerve.
Ligate the left femoral artery with two sutures using 3-0 woven silk just distal to inguinal ligament.
Deliver 200 μl (1 × 10^6 cells) of alginate beads directly to region surrounding the femoral artery.
Close wound with 4-0 Vicryl resorbable sutures.
Monitor the mouse for normal breathing.
Monitor the mouse for normal skin color.
Monitor the mouse for normal posture.
Monitor the mouse for weight loss or gain.
Monitor the mouse for an appropriately healing wound site.
Monitor the mouse for no bleeding, wound dehiscence, signs of inflammation or infection.
Monitor the mouse for signs of pain including tearing and changes in movement or activity level.
Follow recommended post-operative monitoring schedule twice daily for two days following surgery.
Follow recommended post-operative monitoring schedule once per day for the next three days.
Follow recommended post-operative monitoring schedule every other day following the first five days.
Inject 10 mg/kg carprofen subcutaneously every 24 hours for 48 hours following the surgery.
Extend 10 mg/kg carprofen treatment if evidence of pain is observed after the first 48 post-operative hours.
Plug in the heating pad and maintain it at a constant temperature of 37°C.
Connect laser box to power and to camera.
Turn on laser power and adjust to 25%.
Connect the camera to power and to the computer.
Open the camera lid.
Open the speckle pylon software program.
Edit the following parameters in the speckle control panel: Acquisition settings, change # sequence from 2 to 10.
Display settings, check on “enable overlay”, then change raw min = 2.00, max = 250.00; sc min = 0.025, max = 0.11.
Edit file name to reflect mouse sample number and time point (e.g., “m400_d14”).
Change file name for each sample mouse.
Click on “home” icon to choose a path to save file.
Check the files after each mouse imaging session to ensure proper acquisition and saving.
Turn on isoflurane to 2%–5% and oxygen to 1 L/min flow rate.
Place the mouse in the induction box for anesthesia.
Transfer the anesthetized mouse to the nose cone for speckle imaging.
Test laser coverage using a detection card.
Adjust mouse position to expose both paws and make them face up.
Click on camera icon to view live image.
Wait 20 s–40 s to stabilize before starting acquisition.
Click on stop icon, then click on green triangle icon to start acquisition.
Ensure all 10 images are properly saved after 100% progress bar is complete.
Turn off isoflurane and oxygen when imaging session is complete.
Return mice to animal housing.
Close speckle windows.
Set laser power to 0 and power device off.
Disconnect equipment in the following order: Laser power, laser camera connection, camera power, camera computer connection.
Import .sc files into MATLAB.
Run MATLAB script to process speckle data into grayscale.
Export grayscale images into Photoshop or a similar image processing tool, such as ImageJ.
Circle mouse feet to measure the blood flow pixel intensity.
Export data as .csv files and organize into a spreadsheet for each mouse and time point measured.
